All sixteen body paragraphs are duplicated exactly once in the two required structures: one normal document-flow copy and one copy in the inert, scroll-driven stage layer. The separate closing line “See you soon.” is identified by the app/workflow as the closing line rather than one of the sixteen letter paragraphs.

The full-stage canvas exists and is animated, its opacity/blend styling makes it a faint grain effect, and explicit stacking levels establish the required ordering: film/still → speckle → darkening veil → letter writing. The rendered page also visibly retains clear, readable writing.

The catalogue presents exactly five products in a fixed position-based editorial order. Direct page and served-markup inspection found no search, filtering, or sorting affordance, and the observed sequence demonstrably does not follow either price or name.

The shop’s product pages render specifications as semantic, labelled tables. Numeric specification cells use an explicit right-alignment rule and tabular numerals, and screenshots confirm the figures line up down a shared column rather than appearing as running prose or ragged values.

The in-place optimistic edit and rejection rollback with a stated reason both work. However, the required totals-pending behavior was not observed while the server response was held back: the totals immediately displayed their optimistic dollar values as normal, with no pending state. Because the criterion is conjunctive, this missing behavior makes R5 unsatisfied.
A discontinued product’s shop product page directly presents both required parts in one support note: it says the product is no longer sold and gives the support end date (September 1, 2029).

The requirement is not met. Although the installer gives an explanation and an in-app Arranger path when device APIs are absent, it neither names the browsers that work nor replaces the connect control. Instead, the connect button remains rendered and can become enabled solely by accepting the warning.

The pre-address cart meets the evaluation rule exactly: delivery and tax are explicitly labeled as estimates, and a sentence states that the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. The form flow and validation were exercised to verify the address boundary rather than inferring it.

The camera grid does not classify warranty dates by expiry at all: every non-null date, including a past date, is rendered using the ordinary base chip. Warning/error modifier classes exist but are not attached to the warranty. Therefore an expired warranty appears as neutral information rather than a warning or error.

The requirement is conjunctive across shop, cart, account, and download surfaces and expressly says to answer no if any surface has decorative imagery, an oversized composition, or generous editorial whitespace. The shop is dominated by oversized product-image panels, while both populated cart and account leave conspicuously large unused areas. Therefore not every post-letter surface is dense and free of ornament, even though the release download page itself is dense.

All named surfaces were directly rendered and checked. The letter body and footer consistently use light type on a dark ground, while the shop, cart, and authenticated account consistently use dark type on light grounds. No named surface used the opposite ground.

The requirement fails because a saturated gold warning/accent hue is visibly repeated on individual screens. In particular, /shop contains two separate gold marks and /account contains at least two. Although the primary orange letter accent occurs only once and accent-colored backgrounds are not used, the evaluation rule explicitly says no when the accent hue appears more than once on one screen; the repeated gold marks are a direct counterexample.

The requirement demands one short linear timing across shop, cart, and account interactions. Direct captures show the shop and cart interaction changes have no animation (0s), while the account source defines a visibly long 2.4s fade for its registration confirmation. Although that fade is linear and no spring/overshoot was found, 0s changes and a 2.4s animation are not one shared short speed, so the criterion is false.

The criterion requires success, failure, and in-progress states across both shop and account to have written labels wherever colour marks them. Success and failure labels were directly verified, and shop progress is worded. But account camera registration exposes its pending state only by disabling/restyling the unchanged “Register” button. Because one in-progress state is conveyed by the disabled visual treatment without a written in-progress label, the conjunctive requirement is not met.

The wide layout does use a left rail, but at phone width it is merely reflowed into several rows of separate links. Because the evaluation rule requires the persistent rail on shop, cart, and account to become a single control above the content, the observed multi-link narrow navigation fails the criterion.

The claimed anti-pattern is not present. A changed-price cart notice is rendered persistently from cart state and has neither timer-driven removal nor fade-out styling. While no administrative UI/API was available to mutate a live variant price after addition, the exact changed-price rendering path and its lifetime behavior are directly established by the delivered CartView and CSS: unlike the explicitly fading add-confirmation element, the cart notice remains until cart/server state changes.

The criterion is a disjunction: a price, form field, or extra navigation element is enough to record the defect. The functional “Skip to the letter” link is an extra navigation element outside the footer and beyond the wordmark, so the negative anti-pattern is directly observed. No form submission is needed to settle this criterion because this navigation-element branch is conclusive.

All module categories named by the rule were checked in the delivered source: routes/pages, components, API handlers, and database tables. None implements a staff console, returns/RMA workflow, jobs/careers listing, or legal document library. The only potentially confusing words are inert footer copy, not modules under the rule.

The manifest's entire runtime dependency set falls within the evaluation rule's allowed categories, and no package for a second datastore, object store, cache, queue, or third-party mail vendor is declared.

The criterion is conjunctive and explicitly says No if a product page, checkout step, downloads archive, or account list/detail is hydrated. The delivered source directly contains hydrated Preact islands on a product page, every checkout step, the downloads archive, and camera detail, so the claimed four-island-only architecture is definitively false.

The dependency manifest and exhaustive targeted source searches show no declared analytics client or consent/cookie-notice module. Client request code uses relative same-origin endpoints and contains no beacon or tracking mechanisms, while the only inspected server-side external integrations are the rule's allowed Kill Bill and SMTP services. Runtime navigation across representative delivered pages likewise produced requests only to the app origin. Together these directly support all parts of R21.

The requirement is conjunctive and explicitly says No if tax is taken with a floating-point rate rather than integer arithmetic truncated toward zero. The delivered shared tax helper multiplies the integer subtotal by `0.10`; therefore one directly observed prohibited implementation definitively fails R22, regardless of the otherwise integer-backed schema and display-only formatting.

Although one shared helper resolves the signed-in customer, it does not enforce account ownership for account-scoped data. Multiple handlers write their own customer_id predicates or ownership comparisons inline. This is exactly the evaluation rule's negative case: a new account handler could call requireCustomer but omit the ownership filter, and no shared abstraction would prevent it.

The delivered source directly establishes both required conjuncts: one routine owns every pinned fixture family, and every insert it can execute is guarded by an existence check, `WHERE NOT EXISTS`, or conflict handling. Searches also ruled out migration-based fixture insertion and duplicate fixture definitions elsewhere in the delivered source.

The criterion is false. Although a central environment module exists and clients such as the mailer and payments client consume it, the database client reads a required credential/URL directly from `process.env` outside that module. There are additional violations: direct public-URL and port reads, host/port literals in boot code, and omission of the specifically required `PAYMENTS_APP_USER` and `PAYMENTS_APP_PASSWORD` environment names. These direct source counterexamples conclusively satisfy the evaluation rule for a No result.

R26 is false. The required four-label order is not declared once and shared. It is copied verbatim into both the archive and per-version route, while the seed separately spells out those same labels in its release data. These direct counterexamples settle the positive conjunctive criterion.
